images.title: Diagonals 7 cm and 5 cm at 140°
images.purpose: Shows the parallelogram built from diagonals of 7 cm and 5 cm that bisect each other at 140°.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two crossing diagonals in the centre with their ends joined into a parallelogram.
images.exact_structure: Two straight segments crossing at a point O: AC is a thick teal (#0072B2) line, nearly horizontal, and BD is a thick amber (#E69F00) line, shorter, crossing it so that the obtuse angle between them is 140°. O is marked with a small filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) dot. Each half of AC carries one short tick mark and is labelled 3.5 cm; each half of BD carries two short tick marks and is labelled 2.5 cm. One reddish purple arc at O marks the 140° angle, labelled 140°. The four ends are joined in order A, B, C, D by thin dashed grey (#6B7280) lines, making a slanted parallelogram. No corner letters and no side lengths. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Draw the diagonals so they cut each other in half; joining the ends always gives a parallelogram.
images.description: Shows the parallelogram built from diagonals of 7 cm and 5 cm that bisect each other at 140°.
images.context: Halves 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5 cm and 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5 cm; diagonals that bisect each other give a parallelogram.

image_decisions.why: The construction this practice asks for, shown in its finished simplest state.
